Share dedicated deployment pricing + network diagram (Samir)

Jenna: Draft benchmark plan and test script for Emerald infra - due 2026-09-17
David Liu (Emerald): Share current VPC/network peering constraints and data retention targets - due 2026-09-13
meeting_header:
Date: 2026-09-10
Start: 14:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jenna Morales (Redwood SE), Alicia Romero (CISO - Emerald), Ben Carter (Head of ML - Emerald), David Liu (Platform Engineer - Emerald)
summary: Discovery focused on security posture and whether Redwood hosted vs dedicated/private fits Emerald Finance's regulatory and data residency needs. Main areas: SOC2/ISO evidence, SSO/SAML and enterprise SSO integration, RBAC and least privilege model, audit logging/retention, encryption/KMS options, and data retention/deletion policies. Emerald is leaning toward dedicated or private for production but wants to validate SOC2, key management, and network peering. Agreed next steps: Redwood to send SOC2 report, schedule deep-dive to run benchmarks, and share dedicated pricing and network diagram.
topics: Encryption at rest/in transit and KMS integration
Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private tradeoffs
transcript:
[00:00] Samir (Redwood AE): hey everyone, thanks for hopping on, um i'm samir from redwood, i'll kick us off. do you want to do quick intros?
[00:06] Alicia (CISO - Emerald): hi all, alicia here, ciso at emerald finance. listening in to get our security posture questions answered - we operate in finance so compliance is key.
[00:12] Ben (Head of ML): ben here, running ML platform and model infra, curious about latency/cost tradeoffs and how keys are managed.
[00:18] David (Platform Engineer): david, platform eng, i'll focus on networking, peering, and VPC details.
[00:23] Jenna (Redwood SE): jenna from redwood, i'll cover the technical bits - happy to run through architecture and KMS stuff.
[00:28] Samir: cool, thanks. quick agenda: soc2/iso evidence, sso/saml, rbac, audit logs, encryption/kms, data retention, and then next steps. sound good?
[00:34] Alicia: yes. starting with SOC2 - do you have an up-to-date report and is it public? we need type II for our security review.
[00:42] Samir: yep, we do have SOC 2 Type II, we can share the report under NDA; i'll attach the report and penetration test summary after the call. link in notes, i'll also include a whitepaper on our compliance program.
[00:51] Ben: when you say "share," is that the full report or an executive summary? legal usually wants the full attestation.
[00:56] Samir: full attestation, standard redwood practice. we'll get you the doc.
[01:01] Alicia: great. on ISO, are you ISO 27001-aligned or certified?
[01:05] Jenna: we are currently pursuing ISO alignment and have controls mapped; some customers require certification and we have a roadmap - i'll send the control mapping we have today.
[01:13] David: on SSO - we use Okta across the company, integration must be seamless. questions: do you support SAML and SCIM for provisioning and group sync?
[01:21] Jenna: yes, we support SAML 2.0 for SSO and SCIM for automated user provisioning and group sync, RBAC maps to groups. small note: the SCIM endpoint requires a service account and we provide documentation for minimal scopes.
[01:29] Ben: any gotchas with multi-tenant RBAC? we want least privilege per environment and per team.
[01:34] Jenna: RBAC is role-based with per-organization policies; for dedicated/private customers we can enable stricter isolation and custom roles. there are default roles (admin, developer, viewer) and we support custom role claims mapped from SAML groups.
[01:43] Alicia: audit logging - what do you capture? do you provide immutable logs, retention options, and export to our SIEM?
[01:50] Jenna: we capture token-level access logs, model invocation logs (redacted payloads by default), config changes, and auth events. logs are write-once in our backend and can be exported to customer S3 or pushed via secure syslog/forwarder to your SIEM. retention is configurable; default is 90 days on hosted, but for dedicated/private you can set longer windows.
[02:04] David: when you say redacted payloads, does that mean we can opt-in to not store request/response content at all?
[02:09] Jenna: yes - we have an option to disable request/response logging for PII-sensitive workloads. for hosted we redact by default and you can request deletion; for dedicated/private you control log sinks.
[02:17] Ben: encryption - how is data encrypted at rest and in transit, and do you integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM?
[02:24] Jenna: TLS 1.2+ in transit; at rest we encrypt with AES-256. for hosted we use our KMS but offer a customer-managed KMS option for dedicated/private via vault or cloud KMS (AWS KMS, GCP KMS). HSM integrations are available for Private. keys can be rotated and access is logged.
[02:37] Alicia: key access - can we require that keys never leave our control?
[02:41] Jenna: with private deployments you control the KMS and keys; with dedicated we support CMK (customer-managed keys) where key material is in your KMS and Redwood holds only references and uses KMS APIs to encrypt/decrypt.
[02:50] Samir: just to add, for customers wanting full control we usually recommend Private (VPC or on-prem) - that gives the most stringent guarantees around keys and network. Dedicated is a middle ground with isolation and CMK support.
[03:01] Alicia: data residency - do you have region controls and options to pin data to a geographic region? we need european residency for certain workloads.
[03:08] Jenna: yes, region pinning is available for Dedicated and Private. Hosted API has region routing and we can route EU tenant traffic to EU-only regions; for full residency controls Dedicated or Private is recommended.
[03:17] Ben: performance - for inference benchmarks, if we run a test set what are typical latencies for the models you serve? we need 50ms p50 for embeddings in production-ish workloads.
[03:26] Jenna: depends on model and instance type; for smaller embedding models p50 can be under 50ms on dedicated GPU pools with batching. we'll schedule an infra deep-dive to define test harness and traffic patterns.
[03:36] David: networking - we require no public internet access to model serving nodes and peer directly into a VPC. can you support private peering or transit gateway connections?
[03:44] Jenna: yes, we support VPC peering, AWS PrivateLink, and transit gateway for dedicated/private deployments. for hosted we offer VPC egress and secure peering options for enterprise customers. we'll share a network diagram.
[03:55] Alicia: regulatory - any SOC2 scope exclusions? and how often do you refresh certs?
[03:59] Samir: SOC2 scope includes our core inference platform and control plane; we'll include the scope doc when we share the report. certification is annual audit cycle, and controls are continuously monitored.
[04:08] Ben: incident response and breach notifications - what's the SLA to notify customers?
[04:12] Jenna: we have contractual notification timelines for security incidents (standard is 72 hours for critical incidents, we can tighten in enterprise contract). all incidents go through our security team and customers get a post-incident report.
[04:21] David: retention/deletion - we need to be able to auto-delete logs and data after a retention period and to purge data on request. is there an API for that?
[04:27] Jenna: yes, we provide retention policies per org and deletion APIs for data subject requests; for hosted deletion requests are handled by our ops with audit trail, for dedicated/private you can configure automated deletion in your environment.
[04:37] Alicia: tokenization and PII handling - we may want tokens to be stripped before storage.
[04:41] Jenna: available - request/response scrubbing and PII redaction, plus custom scrubbing hooks if you provide patterns.
[04:47] Ben: curious about secrets in prompts - do you recommend client-side masking?
[04:50] Jenna: best practice is to never send secrets; if needed, redact or use placeholders and resolve server-side. we also support prompt pre-processing to remove or hash PII.
[04:58] Samir: ok, sounds like the main blockers are SOC2 evidence, KMS model, and network peering details. are there any other must-haves?
[05:05] Alicia: SSO + SCIM for enterprise onboarding, RBAC mapping, and audit log export to Splunk.
[05:11] Jenna: we integrate with Splunk/Elastic via log forwarders and S3 export; will include configuration examples.
[05:18] Ben: on dedicated vs hosted - cost is a factor, we might start on hosted for evaluation but want to move to dedicated for prod. how do migrations work?
[05:25] Jenna: model pinning and versioning are supported; we provide migration playbooks and data export/import tools. many customers do eval on hosted and then move to dedicated with minimal changes to API.
[05:35] David: if we do dedicated, how long to provision a dedicated GPU pool and networking?
[05:39] Samir: typical lead time is 2-6 weeks depending on region and hardware; we can prioritize in contract.
[05:45] Alicia: one more question on audit logs - do you support tamper-evident logs?
[05:50] Jenna: logs are append-only in our storage, we can support immutability flags and you can ingest into your immutable store if needed.
[05:57] Ben: any known limitations with on-prem private deployments? we have some air-gapped environments.
[06:03] Jenna: air-gapped has extra work - we'll provide an on-prem appliance and offline install docs; telemetry is optional. requires longer lead time and professional services.
[06:11] Alicia: ok - for procurement side we need SLOs on incident response and data deletion timelines included in contract.
[06:17] Samir: noted, we'll include SLA language for incident notification and deletion.
[06:22] David: what's your default retention for embeddings and prompts on hosted?
[06:25] Jenna: default 90 days for logs; request/response content is redacted by default and retention can be set to zero if you choose no storage. embeddings used for caching have configurable TTLs.
[06:35] Ben: do you support customer-side encryption of payloads before sending?
[06:38] Jenna: you can encrypt payloads client-side and provide decryption hooks in your environment; we have customers who do envelope encryption with their KMS.
[06:45] Alicia: regarding cryptographic algorithms - do you support FIPS-140 compliant modules?
[06:49] Jenna: our default stack is not FIPS-validated in hosted but for dedicated/private we can enable FIPS-compliant modules depending on deployment and cloud region. we'll follow up with specifics.
[06:58] Samir: ok, sounds good. who should i send the SOC2 to?
[07:02] Alicia: send to security@emeraldfinance.com and cc procurement.
[07:06] Samir: will do. Jenna, can you own the benchmark and network diagram follow-up?
[07:10] Jenna: yep, i'll set up a technical deep-dive and include step-by-step for peering and KMS options.
[07:15] Ben: excellent. is there any reason we couldn't prototype on hosted? cost vs latency being main tradeoffs.
[07:20] Jenna: you can prototype on hosted; we recommend turning off storing requests and using a smaller model for eval. if later you need predictable latency, we recommend dedicated.
[07:29] David: timeline - we want to decide in Q4, ideally onboarding in Nov.
[07:33] Samir: that aligns, we'll prioritize docs this week.
[07:36] Alicia: ok, that's it from me.
[07:38] Samir: thanks everyone, quick recap in chat: i'll send SOC2 and pen test, jenna will schedule the deep-dive and prepare benchmark plan, i'll share pricing and network diagram for dedicated - any blockers?
[07:49] Ben: none.
[07:50] David: none.
[07:51] Alicia: none.
[07:52] Samir: awesome, thanks all - end call.
[07:54] (call ended)
references: Dedicated deployment network diagram (to be shared)
